Dear Dr Anderson,
Re: Mr Daniel McCrae, DOB 17.10.1962

Thank you for seeing Mr McCrae, a 51-year-old barrister, whose features are suggestive of            Commented [OET1]: Diagnosis already confirmed. You
adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. He requires for further assessment and management.            should use for example “who has been recently diagnosed
                                                                                                     with”

Mr McCrae, who is a smoker, is married with 4 children and he is a smoker. Please note, he has no    Commented [OET2]: His condition

family history of colorectal carcinoma, colonic polyps or inflammatory bowel disease.                Commented [OET3]: Your
                                                                                                     Commented [OET4]: You shouldn’t repeat the subject
Before two weeks, Mr McCrae presented with a several-week history of abdominal discomfort,           with and
flatus, diarrhea, constipation and fatigue. On examination, his vital signs were BP 115/80mmHg, HR   Commented [OET5]: Two weeks ago,
                     ْ
77bpm, Temp 37.1◌, normal and his abdomen was soft, lax with no masses, guarding or rebound
tenderness. Therefore, relevant investigations were requested.

Today, the investigation reports revealed WBC of 8.5, Hb of 91, and Hct of 34%. Additionally, the
fecal occult blood test was positive, and the colonoscopy showed a malignancy in the ascending
colon. Thus, a biopsy was taken which confirmed an adenocarcinoma changes.

In light of the above, Mr McCrae is suffering from adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. It
would be greatly appreciated if you could assess and mange him urgently.

Should there be any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
